records.title: Prices for construction sand in Gasabo skyrocket
records.titleEn: Prices for construction sand in Gasabo skyrocket
records.location: Kigali City, Gasabo District (Rusine, Bumbogo, Jabana areas; Nduba and Kimironko sectors named)
records.summary: Gasabo District authorities suspended sand mining across the district after finding miners operating illegally, pending environmental impact assessments; the article notes local regulations bar sand excavation in wetlands. A New Times mini survey found big crystal sand rose from Rwf50,000 to Rwf75,000 per truckload and small crystal sand from Rwf45,000 to Rwf55,000. District environment officer Peter Barigye said operators had failed to meet minimum requirements set in 2008. A truck driver blamed higher transport costs because sand was now ferried from Bugesera. Nduba Sector said its suspension followed rice farmers' claims that rain-washed sand deposits were burying cultivable soil.
records.limitations: Old (2012) short report; price figures from an informal New Times mini survey; no specific river named (Rusine appears as an area name). Body text loads from the page's embedded article data.

records.title: Gasabo sand miners demand clear policies from leaders
records.titleEn: Gasabo sand miners demand clear policies from leaders
records.location: Kigali City, Gasabo District, Kinyinya Sector
records.summary: Sand miners in Gasabo say unpredictable regulation by Kigali City threatens their business as demand for construction sand grows. Miner Ferdinand Ishimwe said his Kinyinya site, exploiting two hectares and employing some 40 labourers, was closed four times within a year. A labourer with eight years in the trade said he earns Rwf4,000 a day on average. Kinyinya sector executive secretary Remon Berabahizi said the sector, with 15 sites, hosts most of the sand mining Kigali relies on, that many operators leave holes unrehabilitated, and that the sector collects Rwf500,000 per day on average in taxes from sand miners.
records.limitations: No river or wetland is named; the sand pits described are land-based sites in Kinyinya, so the river/wetland link is not stated. Included as context on Kigali construction-sand supply and regulation.

records.title: Rusizi: Abacuruza umucanga ngo babangamiwe no gusora badakora
records.titleEn: Rusizi: Sand traders say they are hurt by paying taxes while unable to work
records.location: Western Province, Rusizi District, Lake Kivu shore (former 'Depo' site, Kubusekanka, Rwinzuki port)
records.summary: Rusizi District closed the lakeside 'Depo' where sand traders worked because it was damaging the Lake Kivu environment, and ordered them to move to Rwinzuki port. At a 2 April 2013 meeting, traders complained the new site lacked road access and berths: one trader said Imuhari has room for one boat while they operate more than 100 boats, and that goods worth 200 million francs had been lost. Mayor Oscar Nzeyimana said 100 million francs had already been spent on Rwinzuki and the Kubusekanka site would close soon. Some traders moved business to Nyamasheke.
records.limitations: Origin of the sand (lake or river) is not stated; loss figures are traders' claims. No byline shown. English translation of the headline awaits native-language review.

records.title: Gucukura umucanga bituma abana bamwe bata amashuri
records.titleEn: Sand digging is making some children drop out of school
records.location: Western Province, Muregeya river on the Rutsiro-Karongi border (Mushubati Sector, Rutsiro; Rubengera Sector, Karongi)
records.summary: Kigali Today reports that children, mostly primary pupils, dig sand in the Muregeya river on the Rutsiro-Karongi border, some abandoning school and others working in holidays. Mushubati Sector executive secretary Etienne Nirere said he knew of the problem and that the children came mostly from neighbouring Rubengera Sector; Rubengera's head said he was unaware and would follow up. Children pool sand to fill a truck and receive 20 thousand francs to share, while the buyer resells the load for 40 thousand francs plus transport. A local digger said efforts to chase the children away had failed.
records.limitations: No count of children; based on local officials and one resident. No byline shown. records.title: Rubavu: Abajabura umucanga baratakamba kubera imisoro ya Njyanama
records.titleEn: Rubavu: Sand diggers protest over district council levies
records.location: Western Province, Rubavu District, Kanama Sector, Kamuhoza Cell (Sebeya river)
records.summary: A Rubavu council decision of 27 June 2016 set the price of a truck of Sebeya sand at 20 thousand francs, split 10 thousand to the district and 10 thousand to diggers. Diggers, who already paid 30 thousand francs a year in tax to RRA, said digging and loading a truck costs them 15 thousand francs, so they work at a loss; Clement Kimenyi of the OTP association said they had bought land to work behind the ten-metre riverbank limit and taken bank loans. Diggers said the work supports about two thousand families. Vice Mayor Janvier Murenzi said costs do not exceed six thousand francs per truck and that riverbed resources belong to the State.
records.limitations: Cost figures conflict between diggers and the district; family count is the diggers' estimate. English translation of the headline awaits native-language review.

records.title: Environment ministry warns against wetland degradation
records.titleEn: Environment ministry warns against wetland degradation
records.location: Kigali City, Gasabo District, Nduba Sector (Nduba wetland)
records.summary: Environment Minister Vincent Biruta launched a special national Umuganda at Nduba wetland in Gasabo to restore marshlands degraded by sand and clay extraction for construction materials, following a May 2018 Auditor General report on wetland threats. Biruta said people had been illicitly extracting sand from the marshland without rehabilitating sites, leaving pits that hold stagnant water and breed malaria mosquitoes, and that permit inspection had not been effective. Nduba Sector executive secretary Providence Musasangohe said some people extract sand secretly at night. The article states Rwanda has 915 wetlands covering close to 10% of the country, 38 of them protected.
records.limitations: Covers sand and clay extraction together; the Auditor General finding cited concerns clay mining specifically. No river named.

records.title: High demand to raise cost of construction materials
records.titleEn: High demand to raise cost of construction materials
records.location: National scope; quarry sources in Rulindo and Muhanga districts supplying Kigali
records.summary: Rwanda Today reports that new district user charges on quarry operators pushed up the cost of building materials, including sand. Operators raised prices by Rwf10,000 to Rwf25,000 per truck of bricks, gravel, sand and stones. A truck of sand cost up to Rwf50,000, up from Rwf35,000 the previous year. A builder and quarry operator said charges and licence costs make building 30 per cent more expensive. Rulindo's vice mayor said fees should not affect prices; quarry proceeds make up over 60 per cent of Rulindo's revenues.

records.title: Nyabihu: Rurageretse hagati ya Koperative na Kampani mu birombe bicukurwamo umucanga
records.titleEn: Nyabihu: Dispute flares between a cooperative and a company over sand-mining pits
records.location: Western Province, Nyabihu District, Nyamutera river
records.summary: A month-long dispute pits the Tunoze Ubwubatsi cooperative against Kigali Trust over construction-sand extraction from the Nyamutera river in Nyabihu. Mayor Antoinette Mukandayisenga says the company holds a valid five-year licence while the cooperative never completed its application. Cooperative members say they were evicted from riverbank land they had developed, losing assets they value at eight million francs. The company says 340 residents work with it without problems. A mining-board inspector says the conflict is a feud between leaders of the 24-member cooperative and the company. The article notes that past corruption suspicions over these pits preceded resignations of district executives.

records.title: Sebeya si umuturanyi mubi - Visi Meya Nzabonimpa
records.titleEn: Sebeya is not a bad neighbour - Vice Mayor Nzabonimpa
records.location: Western Province, Rubavu District, Nyundo Sector, Mukondo Cell
records.summary: Speaking to residents of Nyundo Sector, Rubavu Vice Mayor Deogratias Nzabonimpa said that although the Sebeya floods and destroys homes in the rainy season, the river benefits the district: it supplies treated water, feeds two hydropower plants and provides construction sand used in Goma and Gisenyi. records.title: Kamonyi: Abacukura nta byangombwa bangije ibidukikije ubu barasatira umuhanda wa Kaburimbo
records.titleEn: Kamonyi: Unlicensed diggers have damaged the environment and now threaten the tarmac road
records.location: Kamonyi–Muhanga border: Musambira, Nyarubaka and Kayumbu sectors (Kamonyi) and Cyeza Sector (Muhanga)
records.summary: Unlicensed sand diggers on the Kamonyi-Muhanga border are accused of degrading the environment and undermining the main tarmac road linking Kigali and the Southern Province, with pits less than 3 metres from the road in places. Acting Kamonyi mayor Thaddee Tuyizere said none of the diggers has a permit and they flee when officials arrive; the district was planting flowers along the road to stop them. A resident alleged some officials protect the diggers. Muhanga vice mayor Innocent Kayiranga said most damage is on the Kamonyi side and that permit requests there had been refused.
records.limitations: No river or wetland named; the river/wetland setting of the pits is not stated. Collusion claim is a resident's unverified allegation. English translation of the headline awaits native-language review.

records.title: Amazi ya Nyabarongo ashobora guhinduka urubogobogo - Ubushakashatsi
records.titleEn: Nyabarongo's waters could become clear - research
records.location: Nyabarongo catchment (Muhanga, Gakenke, Ngororero named as mining areas); confluence with Akanyaru in Bugesera
records.summary: Researcher Max Fernandez, who has studied the region for more than 20 years, told Kigali Today the Nyabarongo's muddy colour comes mainly from hillside erosion and mineral mining in Muhanga, Gakenke and Ngororero, and also from clay extraction for Ruliba Clays and sand digging seen in the Nyabarongo valley. He said the water clears after the confluence with the Akanyaru, where the Akagera begins in Bugesera. The article says the Nyabarongo catchment covers 3000 square kilometres across eight districts, and that the national water and forestry agency has a six-year plan focused on erosion control.
records.limitations: Sand digging is a secondary factor in this piece; the researcher attributes most sediment to erosion and mineral mining. 'Six-year plan' is given in words in the original. English translation of the headline awaits native-language review.

records.title: Muhanga: Hari abahanirwa kwangiza ibidukikije ariko ntibisubireho
records.titleEn: Muhanga: Some are punished for damaging the environment but do not stop
records.location: Southern Province, Muhanga District; Cyeza Sector (Biringaga stream); Nyarusange and Cyeza sectors for mineral firms
records.summary: Muhanga District says some miners keep damaging the environment despite fines, and at least five of 19 mining companies were suspended. RMB-seconded staff now help the district inspect sites.

records.title: RIB launches operation to arrest environmental polluters
records.titleEn: RIB launches operation to arrest environmental polluters
records.location: Kamonyi, Muhanga, Gakenke and Ngororero districts (REMA inspection); arrests in Gasabo, Nyarugenge, Gakenke and Ngororero
records.summary: After a Rwanda Environment Management Authority (REMA) inspection from August 8 to August 14 named polluters, Rwanda Investigation Bureau began arresting suspects; spokesperson Thierry Murangira said 19 had been arrested so far, all mining-sector operators. REMA's report found at least five mining companies, five clay mining activities and four sand mining activities in Kamonyi, Muhanga, Gakenke and Ngororero polluting the environment, including causing soil erosion, polluting rivers and wetlands, failing to rehabilitate sites, and ignoring EIA recommendations. Some suspended operators were working without licences.
records.limitations: Sand mining is one of several mining categories; the article does not say which of the 19 arrests concerned sand operators, nor which rivers or wetlands were affected.

records.title: Sebeya River no longer threat to community - Water board
records.titleEn: Sebeya River no longer threat to community - Water board
records.location: Western Province, Sebeya catchment (Rubavu, Nyabihu, Rutsiro; Mahoko, Nyundo, Kanama sector)
records.summary: Rwanda Water Resources Board said restoration of the Sebeya catchment under the Sebeya Project, started in 2019 and costing EUR 15 million, had stopped flood deaths and damage. The article notes that sand mining is carried out along the riverbanks and that authorities want it controlled. The IUCN project manager said mining in the Sebeya for sand and minerals was a main challenge the project did not address, contributing to the river's brown colour, and urged government to improve mining practices in Sebeya and other catchments. About 6,000 community members were involved in terracing, afforestation, dams and dykes.
records.limitations: Sand mining is a secondary point in a catchment-restoration story; no volumes or sites given. Deadly Sebeya floods recurred in May 2023, months after this article.

records.title: Ruhango: Haravugwa amakimbirane mu kwinura umucanga mu mugezi w’Ururumanza
records.titleEn: Ruhango: Conflict reported over scooping sand from the Ururumanza river
records.location: Southern Province, Ruhango District, Mbuye Sector, Gisanga Cell
records.summary: In Mbuye Sector, Ruhango, Theoneste Bimenyimana, who says he scooped sand from the Ururumanza river for more than 10 years, accuses Gilbert Nsengiyumva of taking over his site and his stockpiled sand. Bimenyimana sought renewal of his contract in 2021 but got no answer; the sector says Nsengiyumva received a permit on 20 February 2023 and that Bimenyimana worked without papers. On 21 February 2023 two Howo trucks loaded Bimenyimana's sand, his workers say without payment. Deputy mayor Jean Marie Vianney Rusilibana said Bimenyimana had expanded beyond his authorised area. Sand stockpiled on the banks is trucked to Kigali and elsewhere for construction.
records.limitations: Dispute reported mainly from the parties' accounts; officials do not explain why unlicensed work went unchallenged for over a decade. English translation of the headline awaits native-language review.

records.title: Sand mining business thrives in Western Province
records.titleEn: Sand mining business thrives in Western Province
records.location: Western Province, Rubavu and Nyabihu districts (Mahoko trading centre; Grande Barriere border with Goma)
records.summary: The New Times reports that sand extraction from the Sebeya and Giciye rivers in Rubavu and Nyabihu has become a thriving trade feeding construction in Goma, DR Congo. Official data cited say Nyabihu hosts 37 quarry companies, 27 of them along the Giciye. A Sebeya sand digger, a widow, says she earns at least Rwf 2000 per day. A truckload costs Rwf 80,000 at Mahoko and Rwf 90,000 at the Giciye, rising to about Rwf 480,000 in Goma, and at least 50 heavy trucks cross into Goma daily. RWB's Davis Bugingo says managed extraction can be safe, but illegal mining causes bank erosion, riverbed degradation and buffer-zone encroachment.
records.limitations: Prices and truck counts are estimates without a stated source; the 37/27 company figure is for Nyabihu only. Giciye drains to the Nile side, so the item spans both basins.

records.title: Rubavu: Rurageretse hagati y’Akarere n’umushoramari
records.titleEn: Rubavu: Dispute escalates between the district and an investor
records.location: Western Province, Rubavu District (Intermediate Court of Rubavu); Sebeya river
records.summary: Mugabo J Company Ltd sued Rubavu District at the Intermediate Court of Rubavu after the district halted its sand dredging in the Sebeya despite, it says, full permits. The district said it suspended the firm after clashes between its workers and another company, UStone Ltd. Mugabo J's representative said the district applied new rules of 20/04/2022 to him although his permit was issued on 05/04/2022, while UStone received a permit eight months after rules setting a 300 m spacing took effect, and that district infrastructure claims ignore that he owns 100% of site infrastructure. The hearing was adjourned to 18 September 2023.
records.limitations: Largely one party's account; outcome of the case not reported here. Outlet is a smaller Kinyarwanda site. The '300 m' rule is described only as a spacing distance. English translation of the headline awaits native-language review.

records.title: Western Province issues stark warning against illegal mining
records.titleEn: Western Province issues stark warning against illegal mining
records.location: Western Province; Ngororero District (Kageyo Sector, Satinsyi River photo), Rutsiro, Karongi, Rubavu
records.summary: Western Province Governor Jean-Bosco Ntibitura warned that illegal mining, often for precious minerals or sand from various rivers, threatens the environment and public safety. Police figures cited show provincial illegal-mining cases rose from 167 in 2024 to 206 by August 2025; Ngororero alone reported 83 cases in 2025 and at least 16 fatalities between January 2024 and August 2025. A photo shows miners digging sand in the Satinsyi River, Kageyo Sector. Under the mining law, unlicensed miners face two to five years in prison and fines of Rwf25 million to Rwf50 million; companies face Rwf60 million to Rwf80 million.
records.limitations: Case counts cover all illegal mining (mostly minerals), not sand alone; the sand link rests on the governor's statement and a photo caption. Byline not shown in the page data. Satinsyi drains to the Nile side.

records.title: Ruhango: Hafashwe ingamba zo kuzamura ba nyakabyizi bacukura imicanga na kariyeri
records.titleEn: Ruhango: Measures adopted to uplift casual workers digging sand and quarries
records.location: Southern Province, Ruhango District (district council retreat)
records.summary: At a Ruhango District council retreat, councillors resolved to examine how sand and quarry extraction, which they said is lucrative for investors, could also benefit the casual labourers who scoop sand and load it onto trucks. Council president Jerome Rutagengwa Gasasira said these workers lack stable arrangements and waste their earnings, and proposed a poverty-reduction project forming cooperatives of sand and quarry workers so they could eventually bid for sand and quarry concessions themselves. Southern Province Governor Alice Kayitesi outlined district development priorities.
records.limitations: Policy intention only; no figures, no river or site named, and sand is discussed together with quarrying. English translation of the headline awaits native-language review.

records.title: From Flood Risk to Daily Income: The Nyiramageni Sand Story
records.titleEn: From Flood Risk to Daily Income: The Nyiramageni Sand Story
records.location: Southern Province, Gisagara District, Nyiramageni marshland
records.summary: Under the Rwf16 billion KOICA-funded SAPMP irrigation project rehabilitating the 600-hectare Nyiramageni marshland (with nearly 20 kilometres of canals and sand traps), hillside sediment keeps accumulating in canals. Youths and unemployed residents outside the project's 3,000 farmer beneficiaries manually desilt the sand and load it onto trucks for sale; workers say they extract two to three tonnes per truck and earn about Rwf5,000 per truckload. Sales go through Gisagara District and the Water Users' Association into a cooperative account. Field manager Jean Pierre Muhire says the activity is regulated and taxed at district level. The 2022-2026 project is 86% complete.
records.limitations: Positive, project-centred framing; sand here is desilted canal sediment rather than riverbed mining; income figures are workers' own estimates.

records.title: Plagued by Flooding, an African City Reengineers Its Wetlands
records.titleEn: Plagued by Flooding, an African City Reengineers Its Wetlands
records.location: Kigali City; Nyandungu wetland (eastern Kigali) and Gikondo, Rwampara, Kibumba, Nyabugogo, Rugenge-Rwintare wetlands
records.summary: The magazine reports that Kigali is restoring and reshaping 18,000 acres of degraded wetlands to curb flooding. It says decades of informal agriculture, sand mining and industrial dumping reduced the wetlands' capacity to absorb stormwater. Eastern Kigali's Nyandungu wetland had been despoiled by decades of sand mining, stony quarrying and cattle grazing before REMA began in 2016, at a cost of $5 million, to turn it into the Nyandungu Eco-Park; the park manager says flooding stopped after restoration. Five more wetlands, including Nyabugogo, are being restored.
records.limitations: Sand mining is described as a historical driver of degradation; no current extraction data. Districts are not named in the text.

records.title: Four sand miners killed by flash flood in Muhanga
records.titleEn: Four sand miners killed by flash flood in Muhanga
records.location: Southern Province, Muhanga District, Muhanga Sector, Remera Cell, Kiyoro Village
records.summary: Four men digging sand for sale were killed late on the night of March 12, 2026 in Muhanga Sector, Muhanga District, when a fast-moving stream carrying water, rocks and soil swept through their site close to the Kabere River. Sector executive secretary Telesphore Dusabimana said the men had gone to set their sand trap when large amounts of water came down the stream and buried them; a colleague raised the alarm. Two other young men had been helping dig and sieve the sand. Officials warned residents about the dangers of illegal sand mining and urged caution near rivers during heavy rains.

records.titleEn: HOWO truck stuck in a river for a week
records.location: Southern Province, Muhanga District, Kabacuzi Sector, Sholi Cell, Kinyoni Village
records.summary: A HOWO truck that went to load sand in the Bakokwe stream in Kabacuzi Sector, Muhanga District, had been stuck in the riverbed for a week after the stream rose while it was parked. Sector executive secretary Tharcisse Gihana said no one was hurt and the truck would be removed when the water receded. Jonas Irivuzumuremyi, head of the company licensed to scoop sand in Kabacuzi Sector, said the driver ignored directions to a safer route. records.title: Human-Induced Pressure on the Lake Kivu Shoreline Ecosystem: Evidence from Karongi District, Rwanda
records.titleEn: Human-Induced Pressure on the Lake Kivu Shoreline Ecosystem: Evidence from Karongi District, Rwanda
records.publisher: East African Journal of Environment and Natural Resources (EANSO)
records.authors: Come Niyomuremyi, Christophe Mupenzi, Anaclet Nsanzumuhire, Benjamin Manishimwe
records.location: Western Province, Karongi District, Lake Kivu shoreline (four shoreline sectors)
records.summary: This study assessed human pressure on the Lake Kivu shoreline in Karongi District using a survey of 120 households across four shoreline sectors, key informant interviews, field observation, water-quality tests and GIS land-cover analysis. It identifies agricultural expansion, settlement, tourism, fishing, sand mining and poor waste management as the main pressures. Built-up and farm land expanded and vegetation declined between 2017 and 2024; vegetation loss, erosion, sediment accumulation and waste were key degradation indicators. Water quality showed moderate rather than severe stress.
records.limitations: Abstract only; sand mining is one of six pressures and is not quantified in the abstract. Only the abstract was accessible.

records.title: Geomorphic degradation and heavy metal contamination associated with artisanal alluvial tin and aggregate mining in a Rwandan headwater river
records.titleEn: Geomorphic degradation and heavy metal contamination associated with artisanal alluvial tin and aggregate mining in a Rwandan headwater river
records.authors: Aelis Spiller, Mette Bendixen, Placide Habinema, Jean Pierre Bizimana, and 2 more
records.location: Northern Province, Rulindo District, Rusine River watershed (Rutongo Mining Concession)
records.summary: This preprint studies artisanal alluvial tin and aggregate (sand, gravel, stone) mining in the Rusine River watershed in Rulindo District. Using measurements at 55 sites along a 19km reach and tributaries, the authors found higher riverbank erosion risk at active mining sites, elevated turbidity throughout the main channel indicating catchment-scale sedimentation, and arsenic and chromium in sediments at levels harmful to aquatic life. They note that in the most downstream stretch in-stream sand mining occurs without tin extraction, and that cobbles are also removed to feed stone crushers.
records.limitations: Not peer reviewed (preprint under review). Mixes tin and construction-aggregate impacts; date taken from the page's posted-date metadata.

records.title: Hari abavuga ikimenyane mu gutanga ibyangombwa byo kwinura imicanga no gukura amabuye
records.titleEn: Favouritism alleged in issuing permits to scoop sand and extract stone
records.location: Southern Province, Nyamagabe District, Kaduha and Musange sectors
records.summary: More than five applicants in Nyamagabe's Kaduha and Musange sectors told UMUSEKE their requests for permits to scoop sand and extract building stone were refused while one operator, Mariya Musabyimana, received them through alleged connections to a district official. Buyers of stone from unlicensed pits were fined more than one million francs. Musabyimana said she legally holds 5 permits for sand and stone. Vice mayor Thaddee Habimana said she was licensed on technicians' reports, that RMB monitors permit holders, and that alleged non-compliance with RMB rules would be followed up. Residents say she lacks toilets and worker insurance on site.
records.limitations: Allegations from anonymous applicants; no river named, although 'kwinura umucanga' refers to scooping sand from watercourses. Currency of the fine is not stated beyond 'miliyoni'. English translation of the headline awaits native-language review.

records.titleEn: A 7-year-old child sent to guard rice drowned in a water-filled pit
records.location: Southern Province, Kamonyi District, Rugarika Sector, Sheli Cell, Karehe Village
records.summary: A 7-year-old child sent by parents to guard a rice field after school in Rugarika Sector, Kamonyi District, drowned in a water-filled pit left where sand had been dug, according to sector executive secretary Jean de Dieu Nkurunziza. The child was found dead after failing to return home. Nkurunziza blamed parental negligence and urged residents whose fields have been dug for sand to refill the pits quickly before the rainy season. The body was taken to Remera Rukoma Hospital.

records.title: Nation-wide mapping shows linkages between sand mining activities, human land use, and hydrology in Rwanda
records.titleEn: Nation-wide mapping shows linkages between sand mining activities, human land use, and hydrology in Rwanda
records.publisher: One Earth (Cell Press), via University of Copenhagen Research Portal
records.authors: Ke Huang, Lars Lonsmann Iversen, Rasmus Fensholt, Dimitri Gominski, Martin Brandt, Maurice Mugabowindekwe, Niels Strange, Mette Bendixen
records.dateEvidence: No publication date found on the source page
records.location: National scope
records.summary: This peer-reviewed study applied deep learning to high-resolution aerial imagery to map sand extraction across Rwanda. It reports that mining sites increased by 18% to 3,751 between 2008 and 2023, that sites are spatially linked to river valleys and urban development at sub-watershed level, and that expansion over the past decade often encroached into agricultural areas. The authors present the method as a scalable way to monitor sand extraction and its environmental implications.
records.limitations: Abstract only read on the repository page; the portal gives only the year (2025, vol. 8 issue 3, article 101236), so date set to null. No district breakdown in the abstract. Only the abstract was accessible.
